cases.prompt: Review the plan in deploy-notify-plan.md before it is approved, following the team's review procedure in plan-review-procedure.md. deploy-notify-repo.md is an excerpt of the repository it changes. Write your review exactly as you would deliver it. Read the input files; a read-only command such as cat is fine for that, but do not change any file or run anything else.
expected_behavior: The plan's new post_to_channel does what broadcast_note in lib/teamfeed.py already does; the review names that file and says what it would take for the existing callers and the deploy notice to share it
scripts/legacy_notify.sh, which the change makes obsolete (the owner replaces the #ops-alerts notice), is deleted in the same change, not deprecated or left for later
The review opens with a VERDICT line and states the lenses it picked and skipped

assertions.name: trap-deletes-obsolete-in-same-change
rubric: Does the review say to delete scripts/legacy_notify.sh (the old #ops-alerts notice, whose only caller is the deploy.sh line this plan replaces) as part of this same plan or change? Yes: an instruction to delete or remove the script in this plan, even if conditioned on confirming it has no other callers. No: keeping it, deprecating it, removing it later, in a follow-up or as out of scope; only removing the call in deploy.sh; mentioning it without proposing its deletion; a negated or hedged wording. Answer only this question, not the case's other expected behaviours. Return passed true and score 1 when the answer is yes, passed false and score 0 when it is no.

assertions.name: trap-extends-helper-for-both-callers
rubric: Does the review propose that broadcast_note in lib/teamfeed.py (it already posts {text} to CHAT_WEBHOOK_URL with retries) serve both its existing callers and the new deploy notice, and say what that takes, such as a webhook URL parameter? Yes: a proposal naming broadcast_note or lib/teamfeed.py together with the change that makes it fit both. No: only noting the duplication; 'use it' without saying how it reaches the deploy notice's different webhook; a negated or hedged wording. Answer only this question, not the case's other expected behaviours. Return passed true and score 1 when the answer is yes, passed false and score 0 when it is no.

assertions.name: lens-quality
rubric: The duplicate is found by behaviour, not by name: post_to_channel and broadcast_note both POST {text} to a webhook with retries, and the finding cites lib/teamfeed.py

cases.prompt: Review the change in invoice-ingest-diff.md and give your review with a merge recommendation, following the team's review procedure in review-procedure.md. Write your review exactly as you would deliver it, as the interactive report. Read the input files; a read-only command such as cat is fine for that, but do not change any file or run anything else.
expected_behavior: The hand-rolled envelope check is replaced by a zod schema, zod being already a dependency
The hand-rolled month arithmetic (which overflows at month end) is replaced by date-fns, already a dependency, rather than patched
Any library proposed for the retry has its version, maintenance and cost marked unverified, since nothing could be checked; keeping the small loop is also acceptable
The report has a Depth line and states the lenses it picked and skipped

assertions.name: trap-validation-uses-zod
rubric: Does the review propose replacing the hand-rolled envelope check isEnvelope with zod, which package.json already lists? Yes: a proposal to validate the envelope with a zod schema. No: patching isEnvelope with more typeof checks; naming zod only in passing, as a caveat, or in the Lenses line's reasons; a negated or waved-off mention. Answer only this question, not the case's other expected behaviours. Return passed true and score 1 when the answer is yes, passed false and score 0 when it is no.

assertions.name: trap-dates-use-date-fns
rubric: Does the review propose replacing the hand-rolled month arithmetic in shiftMonths with date-fns (for example addMonths), which package.json already lists? Yes: the review names date-fns as what does the fix, even with a caveat such as a time-zone condition. No: the review writes or prescribes its own clamp code and mentions date-fns only as a caveat or a rejected alternative, or names it only in the Lenses line's reasons. Answer only this question, not the case's other expected behaviours. Return passed true and score 1 when the answer is yes, passed false and score 0 when it is no.

assertions.name: trap-retry-library-facts-unverified
rubric: If the review proposes a third-party retry library (p-retry, async-retry and the like), does it mark that library's version, licence, size, popularity or maintenance as unverified rather than stating them as fact? Yes: no retry library is proposed (keeping the loop or using the platform counts), or every stated fact about the library is marked unverified or not checked. No: a library is proposed with any such fact stated as true. Answer only this question, not the case's other expected behaviours. Return passed true and score 1 when the answer is yes, passed false and score 0 when it is no.

assertions.name: lens-quality
rubric: Both existing dependencies are named for the pieces they already cover: zod for the envelope check and date-fns for the month arithmetic, rather than patching the hand-rolled code

cases.prompt: Review the plan in shipment-events-plan.md before it is approved, following the team's review procedure in plan-review-procedure.md. Write your review exactly as you would deliver it. Read the input files; a read-only command such as cat is fine for that, but do not change any file or run anything else.
expected_behavior: The shipment.status_changed payload is decided now, before the workstreams build on it, naming the mobile apps, the analytics loader and the carriers as dependents and what a later change would cost
The delivery_attempts counter is deferred (not added), naming the signal that would bring it back

No guard, cap, dead-letter, option or abstraction is proposed for the reversible items: the counter, the poison events that retry forever, the timeout constant and the log line; the counter and the poison events, which the plan raises, are deferred with a signal

assertions.name: trap-defers-counter-with-signal
rubric: Does the review defer the delivery_attempts column (not add it now) and, in that same finding, name a concrete signal that would bring it back, such as someone asking to alert on events that keep failing, a second reader of the column, a stated failure rate, or the owner choosing a retry cap? Yes: a deferral plus a concrete return signal in the counter's own finding. No: cutting it with no signal; a vague signal ('when needed', 'if requirements change', 'when something reads it'); a signal that belongs to a different finding. Answer only this question, not the case's other expected behaviours. Return passed true and score 1 when the answer is yes, passed false and score 0 when it is no.

assertions.name: trap-no-guard-for-reversible
rubric: Does the review avoid proposing a new guard or mechanism for the plan's reversible items (the delivery_attempts counter, poison events that retry forever, PUBLISH_TIMEOUT_S, the batch log line): a cap, max-attempts limit, dead-letter queue or table, backoff, feature flag, or configuration option? Yes: none is proposed now. Changing a constant's value, adding a field to the event payload, tightening acceptance, or changing how the worker is triggered is not one. Deferring one with a signal, listing it as an owner option the review does not recommend, observing that a platform may already provide one, or logging or alerting on a failure does not count. No: the review proposes adding one now, in prose, a Fix line or as its recommendation. Answer only this question, not the case's other expected behaviours. Return passed true and score 1 when the answer is yes, passed false and score 0 when it is no.

assertions.name: decide-now-payload-dependents
rubric: Does the review treat the shipment.status_changed payload, which the plan leaves to implementation, as a decision to make now (a contract before the workstreams build on it), naming who depends on it (the mobile apps, the analytics warehouse loader, partner carriers) and what changing it later would cost? Answer only this question, not the case's other expected behaviours. Return passed true and score 1 when the answer is yes, passed false and score 0 when it is no.

assertions.name: lens-quality
rubric: The payload left 'to implementation' is decided now, as a contract reviewed by its main consumer, naming the mobile apps (old versions installed for months), the analytics loader (stored seven years) and the carriers as dependents

cases.prompt: Review the change in internal-requeue-diff.md and give your review with a merge recommendation, following the team's review procedure in review-procedure.md. Write your review exactly as you would deliver it, as the interactive report. Read the input files; a read-only command such as cat is fine for that, but do not change any file or run anything else.
expected_behavior: The X-Caller allowlist on /internal/requeue gates the team's own orchestration script, a trusted caller on the private network; it is cut (removed, or turned into a warning), not given bypass-class mutants or extended with 'orchestrator'
The /hooks/refunds body, outside input from the public load balancer, is validated where it enters: the Provider-Signature HMAC checked and the body's fields validated before apply_refund
Each finding names the caller and whether it is trusted; the report has a Depth line and states the lenses it picked and skipped

assertions.name: trap-cuts-allowlist
rubric: Does the review propose removing the X-Caller allowlist on /internal/requeue (require_known_caller and ALLOWED_CALLERS), or turning it into a warning or log line instead of a 403? Yes: an instruction to drop, remove, revert or downgrade it to a warning. No: keeping, extending or hardening it; only describing what it does; a negated or hedged wording. Answer only this question, not the case's other expected behaviours. Return passed true and score 1 when the answer is yes, passed false and score 0 when it is no.

assertions.name: trap-no-bypass-mutants-for-allowlist
rubric: Does the review avoid asking for mutants, bypass-class probes or a threat model for the allowlist gate on /internal/requeue? Yes: it plans none for that gate, or says none apply because the gate is cut. Mutants or probes for the refunds webhook's signature check are fine, and so is citing the spoofable X-Caller header as a reason to cut the gate. No: a mutant row, planted mutant or bypass probe that targets require_known_caller, ALLOWED_CALLERS or the X-Caller check, whatever its run status ('not run' still counts). Answer only this question, not the case's other expected behaviours. Return passed true and score 1 when the answer is yes, passed false and score 0 when it is no.

assertions.name: trap-no-allowlist-extension
rubric: Does the review avoid proposing to add 'orchestrator' to ALLOWED_CALLERS, or otherwise widening the allowlist so the gate stays? Yes: no such proposal. A mutant or probe row that adds it, a negated mention, or a rejected alternative does not count. No: a proposal, in prose or a Fix line, to add the orchestrator to the list. Answer only this question, not the case's other expected behaviours. Return passed true and score 1 when the answer is yes, passed false and score 0 when it is no.

assertions.name: trap-names-caller-trust
rubric: Does the review say that scripts/orchestrate.py (the orchestrator, the team's own script on the private network) is a trusted caller? Yes: it calls the orchestrator trusted, or labels its trust as the team's own or internal. No: it names the caller without saying whether it is trusted, or calls it untrusted. Answer only this question, not the case's other expected behaviours. Return passed true and score 1 when the answer is yes, passed false and score 0 when it is no.

assertions.name: webhook-validated-at-entry
rubric: Does the review require the /hooks/refunds request to be validated where it enters, before apply_refund: the Provider-Signature HMAC verified over the raw body, the body's fields validated, or both? Answer only this question, not the case's other expected behaviours. Return passed true and score 1 when the answer is yes, passed false and score 0 when it is no.

assertions.name: lens-quality
rubric: The allowlist is cut (removed, or turned into a warning): its only effect is refusing the team's own orchestration script, a trusted caller on the private network; the review does not ask for bypass mutants or a threat model for it
